Subject: Skyline Systems — private interconnect kickoff request

Hi Vivek and Ben,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We're ready to move forward with a private deployment of Redwood in our primary US region. Before we lock dates, the networking and security teams want to validate the interconnect approach (direct VPC peering + private endpoints) and get a short preflight checklist from you.

Primary asks from our side:
- Confirm required subnet ranges and whether we need public IPs for egress.
- High-level BGP/ASN expectations if we go direct connect/partner interconnect.
- MTU and allowed protocols/ports for the private endpoint.
- Any certificates or CNs we need to provision for the private endpoint.

Can we run a 30–45 min technical preflight this week? Carlos (cc'd) will own network details; procurement will follow up separately.

Attachments: skyline_network_diagram_v2.pdf (network team diagram)

Thanks,
Alicia
Senior Cloud Infrastructure Manager
Skyline Systems

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Skyline Systems — private interconnect kickoff request

Hi Alicia — great to hear you're ready. I've sketched a compact preflight plan below so the network/security folks have concrete items to review before the call. Proposed 30–45 min agenda:

1) Topology confirmation (VPC-attachment vs partner interconnect, and preferred route installation)
2) IP addressing & routing (subnet ranges, NAT requirements, BGP ASN if applicable)
3) Private endpoint config (FQDN, cert requirements, SNI, inbound ports)
4) Ops/maintenance (FW rules, MTU, keepalives, monitoring hooks)
5) Implementation milestones & acceptance tests (staging dry-run, cutover, rollback)

Immediate requirements for your network team to pull together before our call:
- Candidate CIDR(s) for Redwood connectivity (suggest: /28 for control plane, /24 for data egress ranges, but we'll confirm sizing based on throughput needs).
- Public ASN (if you plan to peer via BGP). If not, note whether you'd prefer static routes.
- Desired MTU (we recommend 1500 unless you have jumbo frames across the interconnect).
- List of allowed outbound ports: 443 (TLS), 5222 (if you have legacy agent traffic), and UDP 53 for DNS; anything else please list.
- Vault/KMS pattern: will you host certificates or have us provision a trusted cert?

Attachments I'm sharing: redwood_private_install_quickstart.pdf and our interconnect_preflight_checklist.xlsx — these are short. Laura will own the install runbook and will be on the call to capture any network nuances. Monica will lead test/acceptance.

Proposed times (PT): Mon 2/22 10:00–10:45, Tue 2/23 14:00–14:45, Wed 2/24 09:00–09:45. Tell us which works and we’ll send calendar invite.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Implementation
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline Systems — private interconnect kickoff request

Thanks — adding a little more detail on the testing and rollout sequence so Skyline networking knows expectations.

Planned verification steps we will execute during staging and cutover:
- Connectivity checks: ping/traceroute to private endpoint IPs, TLS handshake validation (verify cert CN/SANs), HTTP 200 for health-check path /_status.
- KV cache & latency baseline: run a small tokenized job to validate kv-cache warmup and measure p50/p95 latency.
- Functional smoke tests: 10 sample prompts, verify deterministic responses vs baseline prompt set; report quality regressions if any.
- Failover validation: simulate model fallback to pre-configured variant to confirm application continuity.

Ownership: Redwood CS (Monica) will run the smoke tests and share a short sign-off doc. Skyline to provide a staging VPC and at least one engineer for the live cutover window.

On the call we should also confirm a maintenance window (we recommend a 2-hour window for initial cutover). If you have internal SLAs that conflict, flag them now.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
